title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization
current_update_effect: raw gradient enters both moment estimates and affects the current Adam step through bias-corrected moments
persistent_state_effect: each gradient remains in exponentially decayed m and v and the step counter changes bias correction
detector_signal: none
efficiency_evidence: computationally efficient by design
inclusion_reason: Defines the state carriers and current-versus-persistent decomposition used by every comparison.
audit_notes: Foundational source only; it does not study corrupted labels or selective state protection.

title: TAdam: A Robust Stochastic Gradient Optimizer
current_update_effect: a Student-t weight derived from Mahalanobis distance downweights an outlying gradient in the first-moment update and therefore also attenuates its current parameter effect
persistent_state_effect: the downweighted gradient contributes less to persistent m; raw squared-gradient influence remains in v
detector_signal: Mahalanobis distance under Student-t model using the prior covariance/second-moment estimate
noisy_label_evidence: noise and outlier experiments but not a modern noisy-label PEFT protocol
efficiency_evidence: same asymptotic order as Adam; extra scalar/vector weight operations
inclusion_reason: Closest established prior to selectively robustifying Adam's first moment while retaining an Adam-like second moment.
audit_notes: Its detector is gradient-outlier magnitude under a Student-t model, not label-quality or temporal sign consistency; current and persistent first-moment effects are not separated.

title: DP-AdamBC: Your DP-Adam Is Actually DP-SGD (Unless You Apply Bias Correction)
current_update_effect: subtracts the analytically known DP-noise variance from the second-moment estimate before preconditioning the current update
persistent_state_effect: removes a constant additive DP-noise bias from persistent v while leaving m recurrence unchanged
detector_signal: known Gaussian DP mechanism variance and clipping parameters
noise_rate_required: yes: privacy noise scale is known
extra_forward_backward: one backward plus per-example DP gradient machinery
efficiency_evidence: reported image text and graph tasks; DP overhead is outside this method's incremental correction
inclusion_reason: Shows that corruption can be isolated to one Adam state channel and corrected without rewriting the other, but requires a known noise law.
audit_notes: Not evidence that label noise creates the same additive v bias; its correction is unusable without the DP mechanism's known variance.

title: AdaR: An Adaptive Gradient Method with Cyclical Restarting of Moment Estimations
current_update_effect: the active moment set produces the current update while both active and inactive sets accumulate the raw current gradient
persistent_state_effect: old m and v are discarded cyclically; an inactive set is reset at the interval midpoint and warmed before becoming active
detector_signal: fixed iteration interval rather than a sample-quality detector
noisy_label_evidence: noisy-gradient motivation but no label-noise evaluation
efficiency_evidence: two m/v sets; one RTX A4000; interval tuned by search
inclusion_reason: Direct prior for limiting distant-gradient persistence by moment restart without an extra training stage.
audit_notes: It resets both moments on a clock and does not identify harmful batches; authors leave convergence analysis as future work.

title: SPAM: Spike-Aware Adam with Momentum Reset for Stable LLM Training
current_update_effect: coordinates whose squared gradient divided by prior v exceeds a threshold are clipped before the Adam update, attenuating the current spike
persistent_state_effect: both m and v receive the clipped gradient and are periodically reset; post-reset warm-up controls instability
detector_signal: coordinate spike score g_i^2/v_i plus fixed threshold and reset clock
peft_evidence: indirect: supervised LLM fine-tuning but not noisy-label PEFT
mechanism_evidence: algorithm ablations and state-recovery plots deep-read
efficiency_evidence: slight measured overhead; optional sparse momentum; reset warm-up adds scheduling complexity
inclusion_reason: Strong direct prior for detecting harmful gradients using existing Adam state and preventing their persistence.
audit_notes: It deliberately attenuates the current spike and protects both moments, so it does not implement current-effect preservation or m-only protection; threshold and reset interval require choices.

title: Stable-SPAM: How to Train in 4-Bit More Stably than 16-Bit Adam
current_update_effect: adaptive clipping and matrix normalization alter the current gradient before it reaches the base optimizer
persistent_state_effect: inherits periodic reset of both Adam moments and adds historical gradient-norm statistics
detector_signal: historical maxima and matrix-level norm statistics
efficiency_evidence: runtime and optimizer-memory tables reported for H100 experiments
closest_overlap_class: adaptive spike suppression plus whole-state reset
inclusion_reason: Extends SPAM and demonstrates LoRA compatibility, so it is a required implementation and baseline check.
audit_notes: The arXiv identifier later became GradientStabilizer; the workshop version is therefore anchored to OpenReview and must not be conflated with arXiv v3.

title: GradientStabilizer: Fix the Norm, Not the Gradient
state_target: upstream gradient plus auxiliary norm EMAs; downstream m;v
current_update_effect: replaces the raw gradient norm with the ratio of EMA mean to EMA RMS while preserving instantaneous direction, so current magnitude is changed
persistent_state_effect: the stabilized gradient is written into all downstream optimizer moments; auxiliary norm EMAs persist separately
detector_signal: global gradient-norm variance through two EMAs; no threshold
peft_evidence: no direct PEFT experiment in the verified version
mechanism_evidence: current ICML-version recurrence and bounds deep-read
efficiency_evidence: described as lightweight; adds two scalar norm EMAs and norm reductions
inclusion_reason: Very close low-overhead alternative that bounds moment corruption, though it transforms current and persistent effects together.
audit_notes: Current arXiv v3 is a different method/title from Stable-SPAM v1; version-aware citation is mandatory.

title: Hidden Failure Modes of Gradient Modification under Adam in Continual Learning, and Adaptive Decoupled Moment Routing as a Repair
state_target: m and v receive different gradient versions
current_update_effect: a projected gradient enters m and therefore the current numerator; raw gradient enters v and preserves magnitude-faithful preconditioning
persistent_state_effect: modified and raw signals persist in separate moment pathways; adaptive projection strength depends on protected-subspace overlap
detector_signal: task-boundary low-rank gradient subspace and current overlap energy
clean_reference_required: no clean validation but previous-task structure required
extra_forward_backward: one backward plus buffered-gradient SVD refresh
mechanism_evidence: HTML algorithm recurrence and ablations deep-read
efficiency_evidence: K=50 gradient buffer; randomized SVD; reported below 2 percent wall-clock at tested scales
inclusion_reason: Establishes moment-path decoupling as prior art and is the strongest threat to a broad state-routing novelty claim.
audit_notes: Routes modified gradient to m and raw gradient to v for continual-learning projection; it does not preserve an unmodified current gradient term and requires task boundaries plus subspace machinery.

title: Optimizer Memory Makes Shuffle Order a First-Order Source of Fine-Tuning Noise
optimizer_family: analysis of AdamW momentum and SGD
current_update_effect: no mitigation method; proves equal-multiset order can change the endpoint at first order for fixed-clock optimizer memory
persistent_state_effect: position-dependent impulse weights persist through moment buffers preconditioner and counters
detector_signal: bitwise replay and order swaps
extra_forward_backward: diagnostic replay and HVPs rather than a training method
mechanism_evidence: lifted-state expansion and deterministic replay deep-read
efficiency_evidence: provides seed-budget and replay diagnostics rather than a training overhead claim
inclusion_reason: Supports the causal premise that optimizer memory converts transient order/noise events into persistent effects and constrains seed design.
audit_notes: It is a measurement/theory prior, not a robust optimizer; its result is local to fixed finite windows and does not prove label-noise dominance.

title: Adam on Local Time: Addressing Nonstationarity in RL with Relative Adam Timesteps
current_update_effect: uses a local timestep after known target changes and thereby changes the scale of current Adam updates
persistent_state_effect: the moment buffers remain but their bias-correction clock is reset relative to epochs or target changes
detector_signal: known nonstationarity boundary
efficiency_evidence: drop-in clock change; no extra model pass
inclusion_reason: Relevant control showing that not all optimizer-memory repairs modify moment writes.
audit_notes: Requires observable target/epoch boundaries and addresses RL magnitude shifts rather than stochastic mislabeled samples.

title: Cautious Optimizers: Improving Training with One Line of Code
state_target: parameter update only; m and v unchanged
current_update_effect: after standard m/v updates an elementwise mask removes update coordinates whose optimizer direction disagrees with the current gradient and rescales survivors
persistent_state_effect: raw current gradient is still written normally into m and v, so persistent state is not protected
detector_signal: elementwise sign of optimizer update times current gradient
efficiency_evidence: one elementwise mask and reduction; minimal reported overhead
closest_overlap_class: same agreement signal different intervention point
inclusion_reason: Closest signal-level prior: gradient-momentum agreement is already used, but only at the parameter-update layer.
audit_notes: A candidate using the same sign/agreement detector must claim novelty only from the state-write/current-effect separation and noisy-label evidence, not from agreement itself.

title: Gradient Agreement Hinders the Memorization of Noisy Labels
current_update_effect: updates only parameter coordinates whose gradient directions agree across peer networks
persistent_state_effect: backend optimizer state receives already-masked gradients; no isolated state-write intervention is described
detector_signal: cross-network coordinate-wise gradient sign agreement with class-distribution agreement sampling
noisy_label_evidence: direct synthetic and real noisy-label evidence
mechanism_evidence: official algorithm description and ablations reviewed
efficiency_evidence: training-time comparison reported but three models dominate cost
closest_overlap_class: same agreement signal in noisy labels
inclusion_reason: Kills any claim that gradient agreement is new for noisy-label memorization; differs sharply in model count and intervention layer.
audit_notes: Not compatible with strict single-model low-overhead constraints and does not preserve current gradients while blocking state writes.

title: Early-Learning Regularization Prevents Memorization of Noisy Labels
current_update_effect: adds a regularization gradient to every current update
persistent_state_effect: historical model predictions persist per example and oppose late noisy-label memorization; optimizer m/v are not separately controlled
detector_signal: per-example EMA prediction consistency
extra_models: one for ELR; two for ELR+
noisy_label_evidence: direct synthetic and real noisy-label evidence
efficiency_evidence: ELR is single-model but stores per-example targets; ELR+ is materially heavier
inclusion_reason: Mandatory low-overhead noisy-label baseline because it uses temporal memory without optimizer-state surgery.
audit_notes: Its memory scales with dataset examples and it changes the loss/current gradient; it is not an optimizer-only state mechanism.

title: Towards Robust and Generalized Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Noisy Label Learning
state_target: PEFT activation route; downstream optimizer state
current_update_effect: likely-noisy examples probabilistically bypass PEFT modules so their current gradients to those modules are reduced or absent
persistent_state_effect: because bypassed modules receive no corresponding gradient their optimizer state is also protected, without separating current and persistent effects
detector_signal: previous-epoch loss GMM and stochastic per-layer routing
clean_reference_required: no mechanism-level clean reference; tuning caveat remains
extra_forward_backward: extra consistency forwards with cached ensemble predictions
peft_evidence: direct across Adapter BitFit prompt tuning and LoRA
efficiency_evidence: no complete end-to-end wall-clock or VRAM comparison
closest_overlap_class: PEFT routing blocks current and state together
inclusion_reason: Closest application prior for protecting PEFT capacity from noisy exposure under unknown noise rate.
audit_notes: Does not operate specifically on Adam moments and does not preserve the current noisy example's parameter effect.

title: Why LoRA Resists Label Noise: A Theoretical Framework for Noise-Robust Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
current_update_effect: both low- and high-rank adapters are trained; current gradients are not separated from optimizer state
persistent_state_effect: rank-specific training histories create a discrepancy used for noise detection and optional retraining
detector_signal: loss discrepancy between low- and high-rank adapters
noise_rate_required: threshold may use estimated noise rate
efficiency_evidence: roughly doubles training time before optional retraining
inclusion_reason: Strong 2026 PEFT-specific temporal prior, but much heavier than an optimizer-state plug-in.
audit_notes: Single-author preprint with restrictive theory assumptions; not evidence for m-only state control.

title: Weed Out, Then Harvest: Dual Low-Rank Adaptation is an Effective Noisy Label Detector for Noise-Robust Learning
current_update_effect: current examples affect clean and noisy adapters under opposite temporal constraints
persistent_state_effect: separate adapter memories drive a detector before downstream retraining
detector_signal: per-sample clean-versus-noisy adapter loss difference plus external labels
clean_reference_required: yes: clean development set and GPT-4o support
extra_models: dual adapters plus downstream classifier and GPT-4o
noisy_label_evidence: direct synthetic and real noisy-label text evidence
efficiency_evidence: dual adapters and external-model calls; cost not fully accounted
inclusion_reason: Kills broad claims around temporal LoRA separation but violates the strict self-contained low-cost contract.
audit_notes: Must be described as using GPT-4o twice and clean-development tuning; not an optimizer-state baseline.

title: Handling Label Noise via Instance-Level Difficulty Modeling and Dynamic Optimization
current_update_effect: stage two reweights supervised pseudo-label and two-view consistency gradients by inferred cleanliness and difficulty
persistent_state_effect: persistent sample history and mixture fits shape future losses; optimizer state is downstream and not isolated
detector_signal: wrong-event counts plus class-wise beta mixture
extra_forward_backward: two augmented forwards in stage two
noisy_label_evidence: direct synthetic and real noisy-label evidence
efficiency_evidence: reported per-epoch seconds and VRAM on A100; five plus ten epochs
inclusion_reason: Main strong recent baseline against claims based only on cheap temporal statistics.
audit_notes: Two-stage and two-view costs differ from a one-pass optimizer plug-in.

title: MGUP: A Momentum-Gradient Alignment Update Policy for Stochastic Optimization
optimizer_family: plug-in for AdamW Lion and Muon
current_update_effect: uses momentum-gradient alignment to assign larger or smaller nonzero step sizes to a fixed proportion of parameter coordinates
persistent_state_effect: base optimizer state formation is not the selected intervention target
detector_signal: momentum-gradient alignment and fixed selection proportion
mechanism_evidence: abstract and official preprint metadata reviewed
efficiency_evidence: claimed plug-in overhead; full wall-clock not yet deep-audited
inclusion_reason: Recent direct terminology and signal threat; must be separated from state-write gating.
audit_notes: Preprint appeared in June 2026; current evidence does not establish selective protection of Adam moment writes.

title: Adaptive t-Momentum-based Optimization for Unknown Ratio of Outliers in Amateur Data in Imitation Learning
current_update_effect: extends t-momentum with automatic robustness so outlying demonstrations are downweighted in current optimization
persistent_state_effect: robust first-moment accumulation reduces persistence of imperfect demonstrations
detector_signal: adaptive Student-t heaviness estimate
mechanism_evidence: official abstract and TAdam lineage reviewed
efficiency_evidence: Adam-like pass count; adaptation details require baseline implementation audit
inclusion_reason: Shows TAdam's first-moment robustification was already extended to unknown outlier ratios.
audit_notes: Application is behavioral cloning and not PEFT; still a direct mechanistic prior for unknown-contamination settings.

title: Rethinking Adam: A Twofold Exponential Moving Average Approach
state_target: v is driven by squared m
current_update_effect: current raw gradient first updates m; the current step uses m divided by a v formed from squared momentum rather than squared raw gradients
persistent_state_effect: all gradients persist through m and v with coupled recurrences; no quality gate
detector_signal: none beyond momentum smoothing
efficiency_evidence: no extra passes or models
inclusion_reason: Necessary structural control because it changes which signal writes v and couples the two state channels.
audit_notes: It does not detect contamination or block a harmful sample; it replaces raw-gradient v input for every step.
